name: alarm
description: The alarm tool's whole lifecycle in one pass: set must persist a reminder and return its id, list must show it as pending with due:false, cancel must remove it, and a second list must come back empty. Exercises the tool's CAS read-modify-write path against state/alarms.json end to end — application logic no build gate touches. It goes red when set stops persisting, ids stop round-tripping to cancel, or a stale-hash retry loop breaks. The eval's staging state dir starts empty, so the final empty list is deterministic.
prompt: Use the alarm tool four times, in order: (1) {"action":"set","message":"eval reminder","in_minutes":60}; note the id it returns. (2) {"action":"list"} — check the alarm you just set is present with due false. (3) {"action":"cancel","id":"<the id from step 1>"}. (4) {"action":"list"} — check the alarms array is now empty. If every step behaved as described, reply with exactly CLEAN. Otherwise reply with exactly BROKEN and one sentence naming the failing step.
